# Page 15^page=15
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 15 Daily Content PDF NATIONAL AFFAIRS MoRD Notifies Grievance Redressal Rules,2026 for VB-G RAM G Scheme In November 2026, the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD) notified the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB–G RAM G) Grievance Redressal Rules, 2026, under the VB–G RAM G Act, 2025, to establish a structured, transparent and time-bound grievance redressal mechanism for the rural employment scheme. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Notification of Grievance Redressal Rules, 2026 ✓ For? VB-G RAM G Scheme ✓ Notified by: MoRD ✓ Key Features: o Multi-tier redressal system (GP, block and district level); o Stringent timelines (7 days for completion of investigation and 15 days for complete disposal of grievances); o Key Provisions Omitted: Registration of FIR in cases with prima facie evidence of embezzlement; and submission of action-taken report before the GPs. About Grievance Redressal Rules 2026: Multi-tier System: The new grievance redressal rules has directed the state to establish grievance redressal mechanisms at Gram Panchayat (GP), Block and District levels. Managed by: MoRD has designated Grievance Redressal Officers (GROs) at the appropriate levels, who will be mainly responsible for receiving, registering, enquiring into and resolving grievances. • At district-level, the District Programme Coordinator (DPC) will oversee grievance redressal to ensure that grievances are addressed through the designated mechanism and the Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) for grievance redressal. Timelines: The newly notified rules prescribed strict timelines for resolving the grievances i.e. completion of investigation within 7 working days from the date of receipt and final resolution within 15 days. Escalation of Unresolved Complaints: The complaints that remain unresolved after 15 days will be automatically escalated through digital platforms for redressal of grievance to the next higher-level. • Such complaints will continue to be monitored digitally until they are disposed of. Mode for Registration of Complaints: The new rules allows any person to submit a complaint concerning the implementation of the scheme, either orally or in writing. • Digital Registration: Complaints filed physically at all 3-levels must be registered on the digital platform on the day they are received or, where this is not feasible, by the next working day. • Acknowledgement of Complaints: Every registered complaint receives an acknowledgement containing a registration number, the date of receipt and the designation of the receiving authority. • No Refusal: The designated officers cannot refuse to register/oversee grievances based on format, language, manner of submissions, or procedural errors.

# Page 16^page=16
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 16 Daily Content PDF Appeals: The aggrieved party/person can appeal against decisions under the grievance redressal mechanism. Such appeals will be handled in accordance with clauses (i) (j) and (k) of paragraph 28 schedule I to the VB-G RAM Act, 2025. Omission of Key Provisions of MGNREGA: The MoRD has omitted two previous provisions of the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA): • The mandatory requirement to register an First Information Report (FIR) when preliminary inquiries or social audits revealed prima facie evidence of financial irregularities; • Requirement to submit action-taken reports on grievances before panchayat and district panchayat meetings for review and monitoring. About Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB–G RAM G): Repealed MGNREGA: The VB-G RAM Act, 2025 repealed the MGNREGA, 2005, starting from July 1, 2026. Extended Employment Guarantee: The new act provides a statutory guarantee of 125 days of work in every financial year (up from the provision of 100 days in MGNREGA, 2005) to every household whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work. Wage Payments: Under the scheme, wages to labourers are disbursed through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) into their bank or post office accounts. • Also, payments are processed within three days, ensuring that all procedures are completed and the funds reach their accounts within a maximum time period of 15 days. • However, if the funds are not received within 15 days, workers are entitled to receive delayed payment compensation. • Further, workers are entitled to get an unemployment allowance, if employment is not provided upon demand. About Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD): Union Minister- Shivraj Singh Chauhan (Constituency- Vidisha, Madhya Pradesh, MP) Union Minister of State (MoS)- Chandra Shekhar Pemmasani (Constituency- Guntur, Andhra Pradesh, AP); and Kamlesh Paswan (Constituency- Bansgaon, Uttar Pradesh, UP) MSDE Partners with Assam to Establish SIIC; Signs LoIs for Two ITI Clusters Under PM-SETU On 2 November 2026, the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) organised the ‘Skilling for International Mobility & Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) programme in Guwahati, Assam, focusing on the Tourism and Hospitality sector. • During the programme, MSDE announced a partnership with the Government of Assam to establish a Skill India International Centre (SIIC) and signed Letters of Intent (LoIs) for upgrading two Industrial Training Institute (ITI) clusters under the PM-SETU scheme. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Skilling for International Mobility & PM-SETU ✓ Organised By: MSDE ✓ Where? Guwahati, Assam ✓ Focus Sector: Tourism and Hospitality ✓ Partnerships Announced:

# Page 17^page=17
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 17 Daily Content PDF o MoU for SIIC: MSDE + Government of Assam o LoI for Jorhat ITI Cluster: Supported by NRL o LoI for Tinsukia ITI Cluster: Supported by OIL About the Programme: Objectives: Strengthening the North-Eastern Region’s skilling infrastructure, expanding international employment opportunities and transforming ITIs through industry participation. Participation: Bringing together representatives of the Central and Assam Governments, industry stakeholders and the skilling ecosystem, with a special focus on the Tourism and Hospitality sector to address the growing demand for skilled professionals in domestic and international markets. Key Partnerships and ITI Cluster Development: SIIC: The MoU between MSDE and Government of Assam aims to establish a SIIC in Assam to strengthen international workforce mobility by providing industry-aligned training, internationally recognised certifications and pathways to overseas employment, while preparing young people to meet global industry requirements. PM-SETU: LoIs were signed for two ITI clusters at Jorhat and Tinsukia in Assam under the PM-SETU scheme, with support from Numaligarh Refinery Limited (NRL) for Jorhat and Oil India Limited (OIL) for Tinsukia. Transformation: The partnerships aim to strengthen industry participation and promote industry-led transformation of the vocational education and training ecosystem in the North- Eastern Region by converting ITIs into modern, demand- driven and industry-responsive institutions aligned with emerging workforce requirements. About PM-SETU Scheme: Overview: The PM-SETU scheme is a flagship, Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) for vocational education, launched by the Government of India (GoI) on 4 October 2025, which completed its first year of implementation in October 2026. Implementation: The scheme is implemented by the Directorate General of Training (DGT) under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE). Objectives: The scheme aims to restructure and modernise India’s vocational training network in alignment with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 and the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. Outlay: The scheme has a total financial outlay of Rs. 60,000 crore over five years, with contributions from the Central Government (Rs. 30,000 crore; 50%), State Governments (Rs. 20,000 crore; 33.3%) and industry partners (Rs. 10,000 crore; 16.7%). • The scheme includes co-financing support from the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and the World Bank (WB) towards the Central Government’s share. About Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE): Union Minister of State (MoS) (Independent Charge, IC) – Jayant Chaudhary (Rajya Sabha member- Uttar Pradesh, UP) PM Narendra Modi Inaugurates and Lays Foundation Stone of Pune Metro Projects worth around Rs 21,800 Crore In November 2026, Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi inaugurated and laid the foundation stone for Pune Metro projects (Maharashtra) worth around Rs 21,800 crore via video conferencing.

Background: First Edition: The first edition of Exercise Tiger Triumph was held in November 2019 near Visakhapatnam and Kakinada, AP, marking the beginning of India–USA Tri-Service cooperation in HADR operations. 4th Edition: The previous edition of the exercise was conducted from 1 to 11 April 2025 at Visakhapatnam and Kakinada, AP. About Exercise Tiger Triumph 2026: Format: The exercise is being conducted as a Tabletop Exercise (TTX) to strengthen joint planning, coordination and interoperability between the Armed Forces of both countries during large-scale disaster relief operations Focus: The exercise aims to facilitate Combined Joint All-Domain Operations, strengthening cooperation across multiple operational domains during humanitarian emergencies. Participation: • Indian Contingent: The Indian contingent comprises specialists from the Indian Navy (IN), ground personnel from the Indian Army (IA), representatives from the Indian Air Force (IAF) and Special Forces from all three Services. IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, Jharkhand ✓ Purpose: Strengthen collaboration in critical and strategic minerals sector ✓ Other Launch: NITI Aayog launched India S&T Scoreboard ✓ Objective: To support evidence-based S&T policymaking and State benchmarking. About NITI Aayog-TEXMiN SoI: Agreement: The SoI was signed during the visit of Prof. Gobardhan Das, Member, NITI Aayog, to Indian Institute of Technology (Indian School of Mines) [IIT (ISM)] Dhanbad, Jharkhand, where he inaugurated the National Symposium on Critical Minerals and Rare Earths (CMRE 2026), held as part of the 45th Annual National Conference of the Indian Council of Chemists. Focus: The partnership covers four areas: collaborative research and technology development, technical and strategic studies, policy and institutional support, and capacity building and knowledge exchange to strengthen India’s critical minerals ecosystem. Value Chain: An integrated value chain covering exploration, processing, refining, advanced materials and recycling, with critical mineral recovery from coal fly ash, red mud, mine tailings and electronic waste, will promote indigenous technologies and sustainable resource utilisation. About TEXMiN: Established in 2020 as a Technology Innovation Hub (TIH) under the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Ministry of Science and Technology (MoS&T), it was upgraded to a Technology Translation Research Park (TTRP) at IIT (ISM), Dhanbad, Jharkhand. NITI Aayog Launches India S&T Scoreboard: In November 2026, Ashok Kumar Lahiri, Vice Chairman of NITI Aayog, launched the interactive India Science & Technology (S&T) Scoreboard at the Civil Services Officers’ Institute (CSOI), KG Marg, New Delhi, Delhi. Objectives: The platform provides an integrated overview of the science and technology landscape across Indian States and Union Territories (UTs), enabling evidence-based policymaking, performance benchmarking and identification of research and innovation strengths and gaps. Coverage: The Scoreboard consolidates data on higher education institutions, Research and Development (R&D) institutions, deep-tech startups, incubators, research publications and patents across three sectors: Academia, Government R&D Laboratories and Industry. Significance: Guided by cooperative and competitive federalism, the platform enables State comparisons, identifies strengths and gaps, promotes best-practice sharing. About National Institution for Transforming India (NITI) Aayog: Chief Executive Officer (CEO) – Anurag Jain Headquarters – New Delhi, Delhi Established – 2015 Bihar Becomes First Indian State to Introduce Comprehensive Silt Management Policy, 2026 On 3 November 2026, Bihar Chief Minister (CM) Samrat Choudhary highlighted the Bihar Water Sources Restoration and Silt Management Policy, 2026, notified on 17 September 2026, making Bihar the first state in India to formulate a comprehensive state-level silt management policy.

Exam Hints: ✓ What? Bihar Water Sources Restoration and Silt Management Policy, 2026 ✓ First State: Bihar ✓ Announced By: CM Samrat Choudhary ✓ Objective: Scientific desilting, river restoration and flood management ✓ Nodal Department: Road Construction Department (RCD), Bihar ✓ Related Initiative: Nadi Sanjivani ✓ MoU Partners: MoRTH and Government of Bihar. About Comprehensive Silt Management Policy, 2026: Background: Rivers originating in Nepal carry substantial quantities of water and sediment into Bihar, making the state vulnerable to recurring floods. Continuous silt accumulation reduces river-carrying capacity, obstructs water flow and affects agricultural land. Agricultural Protection: The policy allows removal of sand and silt deposited on farmland after floods and promotes the use of excavated sediment in construction instead of fertile topsoil. Implementation: Bihar’s Road Construction Department (RCD) will coordinate the initiative with NHAI, supported by a State-level Coordination Committee. Nadi Sanjivani Initiative: the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) and the Government of Bihar signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to promote scientific desilting and reuse of extracted silt in National Highway projects. INTERNATIONAL AFFAIRS QS World University Rankings Asia 2027: The University of Hong Kong Tops; IIT Delhi Slips to 66th In November 2026, global higher education analyst Quacquarelli Symonds (QS) released the QS World University Rankings: Asia 2027, revealing that 71% of previously ranked Indian universities declined in their positions, despite India’s strong performance in research productivity and doctoral education. • Mainland China led in representation with 448 universities, followed by India (325) and Japan (153), while the University of Hong Kong topped the rankings, followed by Peking University and Tsinghua University. • Indian Institute of Technology Delhi (IIT-D) was India’s highest-ranked institution at 66th, with 34 new Indian entrants. Exam Hints: ✓ What? QS World University Rankings: Asia 2027 ✓ Released by: Quacquarelli Symonds (QS) ✓ Coverage: 1,722 universities across 26 higher education systems ✓ Top 3 Most Represented Countries: Mainland China (ranks 1st, 448 universities); Indian (ranks 2nd, 325 universities); and Japan (ranks 3rd, 153 universities) ✓ India’s Highest-Ranked Institution: IIT Delhi (66th) ✓ Asia’s Top University: University of Hong Kong QS World University Rankings (Asia) 2027: Coverage: The latest edition of the rankings featured 1,722 universities across 26 higher education systems, with 195 new entrants. Methodology: Published annually since 2009, universities are ranked based on their performance across 11 indicators such as: • academic reputation (30%); employer reputation (20%); faculty/student ratio (10%); international research network (10%); citations per paper (10%) and paper per faculty (5%); staff with Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) (5%); proportion of international faculty (2.5%) and proportion of international students (2.5%); • Proportion of inbound exchange students (2.5%) and proportion of outbound exchange students (2.5%). Top Ranked Asian University: The University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR) China with an overall score of perfect 100 retained the top position in 2027 rankings for the 2nd consecutive year.
